name: 1626 Prairie Avenue: the brick stable on the alley, K12

function.note: The 1911 sheet draws the building crossed by one X, the key's sign for a stable (the T-1840 census: '2-storey brick stable (X) on the alley'), and Robinson's 1886 plate 10 crosses the brick building it draws on the same ground, the atlas's stable. Carried to 1904 between the two, INFERRED; no source names a horse or a carriage on this lot.

research_note: T-1932 refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, beside 1628's stable (the two share one wall on the sheet). The sheet census (census row s20-1626-r1, trace s20fp-1626-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. The kit is built in mirror image (`mirror`), its party wall at the south end on the wall line it shares with 1628's and its open gable, with the sheet's two-dot window mark, to the north, facing the open rear of lot 15. Robinson's 1886 plate draws the same pair of crossed brick stables at nearly the same sizes, so this one stood from before 1886 through 1911. No picture of it is known. The reading is in docs/RESEARCH/k12-1626-1628-stables-1932/README.md.

documented_range.note: STANDING IN 1904 rests on two maps either side of it. Robinson's 1886 plate 10 draws a pink, crossed building on the alley across the rears of lots 16 and 17 in two parts, each about 7.3 m along the alley (pink-density profiles on the committed plate raster at its 0.346 m a pixel: rows 1222, 1243 and 1264.6), the north part about 11.1 m deep (columns 342-374) and the south part about 14.5 m (columns 341-383): within the plate's line widths, the two buildings the 1911 sheet draws, 1626's 7.97 by 11.87 m and 1628's 7.01 by 13.94 m. The 1911 sheet draws it again, so it stood from before 1886 through 1911 and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), as the district draft did. FROM: the record claims the 1904 target and no earlier day. TO: the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; none reads a 1911 Sanborn sheet. This position is pixel (2225.57, 2868.5) of the committed sheet 20 raster carried through the similarity in data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json (local_e = a*px + b*py + c, local_n = d*px + e*py + f) plus the datum origin, and the note carries the pixel and the result so the sum can be recomputed by hand.

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (into the lot) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 2225.6) to its east wall line (2459.3) and from its north wall line (row 2790.1) to the wall line it shares with 1628's building (2947.0), each the peak of a median darkness profile: 233.7 by 156.9 pixels at the sheet's 0.050779 m a pixel, 11.869 m deep by 7.967 m along the alley. The district draft's fit found a 6.0 by 10.75 m rectangle inside the traced part.

stories.note: '2' lettered on the building: two storeys.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, with wall thicknesses lettered '12 8' (inches, the first storey's and the second's, as the key reads them) inside its north wall and again on the wall line it shares with 1628's. Robinson's 1886 plate also colours it pink, its brick.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the sheet's two window marks is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1626-1628-stables-1932. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 8', a stable's X, and two of the key's window marks, each with a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there): on the alley wall about 4.06 m from the north wall line, and on the north wall about 3.12 m from the alley line. It draws no fire-wall sign on this building. The kit is built in MIRROR IMAGE (`mirror`, as at 1612): its party wall stands at the south end, on the one wall line the sheet draws between this building and 1628's, and its open gable at the north end, which faces the open rear of lot 15 and carries the sheet's north-wall mark. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face (the alley and yard walls' s from the south end and the north end respectively, as the kit lays them; the gable's from the alley face). The alley wall carries a stable sash and a loft sash over it where its mark stands, a man door with a loft sash over it toward the south end, and the kit's carriage bay at its narrowest (2.7 m clear) toward the north end with the loft hatch over it; the yard wall a door onto the workyard at its middle between two stable sash and two loft sash; the north gable a stable sash and a loft sash over it where the sheet's mark stands. The south end's party wall rises the kit's 0.45 m above the roof, where the sheet draws no fire-wall sign: it is the wall shared with 1628's, whose own party wall the kit stands back to back with it. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees (1616's, 1612's and 1736's deep-stable pitch) over the 11.87 m span, about 3.4 m from eave to ridge. No external stair, ramp, lean-to, wing or ventilator: the sheet draws none. Not built: the sheet's solid dot inside the building about 1.4 m from its south wall and 6.3 m from the alley, the key's sign for a vertical steam boiler (the kit has no stack, and the sheet draws none). The workyard is paved from the yard door to the house's rear porch, 5.9 m east of the yard wall.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and workyard are the kit's, laid out for this lot with the sheet's two window marks where it puts them, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.
